faq.lead: Can’t find your answer? The app itself tells you what is wrong and which button fixes it. Open the service or link details first.

items.q: Is Loggia free?
items.a: The free plan is. It can publish up to 2 services to the internet and can’t turn on new access protection. Pro removes these limits, as a one-time purchase. See Pricing.

items.q: What do I need?
items.a: A Mac with macOS 26 or later, a Cloudflare account, and at least one domain managed by Cloudflare.

items.q: Do I have to pay Cloudflare?
items.a: Publishing uses Cloudflare Tunnel, which is free. Access protection needs Zero Trust set up on your account, and the free plan is enough. Your domain is billed by its registrar as usual.

items.q: Does my Mac have to stay on?
items.a: Yes. Your services keep running on your Mac; Loggia only gives them a public address. While the Mac is asleep, off or offline, the address can’t be reached. The connector starts at login, so services come back as soon as your Mac does.

items.q: Does my traffic go through your servers?
items.a: No. Visitors reach your services through Cloudflare, straight to your Mac. Loggia has no servers of its own and does not see your traffic. See the Privacy Policy.

items.q: Which permissions does the API token need?
items.a:
In onboarding or in Settings › Cloudflare, click Create a Token on Cloudflare. It opens a template with the permissions already selected, so you only need to confirm it. The template includes:

Account › Cloudflare Tunnel › EditRequired
Zone › DNS › EditRequired. Zone Resources can be limited to the domains you use.
Account › Access: Apps and Policies › EditOptional, for access protection
Account › Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups › EditOptional, lets Loggia set up the email-code login for you

Settings › Cloudflare lists each permission and has Copy Permission List if you prefer to create the token yourself. The token is stored only in your Mac’s keychain.

items.q: I just fixed the token’s permissions, but Loggia still says they’re missing.
items.a: Changes on Cloudflare take a minute or two to take effect. Wait a moment, then click Check Again in Settings › Cloudflare.

items.q: Why can’t I turn on access protection?
items.a:
• Access protection is a Pro feature.
  • The service has to be published first.
  • The token needs both Access permissions listed above.
  • Your Cloudflare account needs Zero Trust set up. The free plan is enough. Once it is set up, click Check Again in Settings › Cloudflare.

items.q: With access protection on, who can open my service?
items.a:
Only the email addresses you list, or everyone at a domain if you add @example.com. Visitors get a one-time code by email. A login lasts 24 hours by default, and you can change that.

With Pro you can also add trusted networks, such as your home or office internet address. Visitors from a trusted network open the service without the code, and so does anyone else on the same Wi-Fi or mobile network.

items.q: Will Loggia overwrite a domain I already use?
items.a: Not silently. If the domain already points somewhere else, Loggia stops and asks you before changing anything.

items.q: How many Macs can use one license?
items.a: Two. To use it on a different Mac, first click Deactivate in Settings › License on one of the Macs that has it.

items.q: Does Pro need an internet connection?
items.a: Activating needs one. After that Loggia checks the license once a day. If it can’t reach the license server, Pro keeps working for 30 days after the last successful check, and comes back on its own once the Mac is online again.

items.q: Which versions does a license cover?
items.a: All 1.x versions. Updates themselves are free on both plans.

items.q: Can I get a refund?
items.a: Yes, within 14 days of buying. The Refund Policy says how to ask and what happens to your license.

items.q: What happens after a refund, or if a license stops being valid?
items.a: Loggia goes back to the free plan, and nothing is taken offline: services you published keep running. The free plan manages only the first 2 published services in your list. The others keep running, but Loggia stops checking them and shows them as Not managed; you can still stop publishing them. Access protection that is already on keeps working; you can turn it off but not change it. Upgrading to Pro again restores everything.

items.q: A service shows as down. Where do I start?
items.a: Open the service. Loggia shows which part of the link is broken (your local service, the domain record, the connector on your Mac, or Cloudflare), why, and the button that fixes it. A new domain record can take a few minutes to take effect.

items.q: Loggia says a proxy app is intercepting the connection.
items.a:
In enhanced or TUN mode with fake IP, a proxy app answers for argotunnel.com with fake addresses, so cloudflared keeps at most two connections to Cloudflare, or none. When cloudflared can’t reach Cloudflare, Loggia checks for this and only then names a proxy app. In the proxy app:

  1. Route argotunnel.com and cftunnel.com directly.
  2. Add +.argotunnel.com to the fake-IP filter (fake-ip-filter), so it resolves to Cloudflare’s real addresses. In fake-IP mode a direct rule alone is not enough.
  3. Click Reconnect, Try Again or Restart, whichever Loggia shows.

The status of your public services is checked from the internet and is not affected by the proxy app. If a domain you just published opens elsewhere but not on this Mac, the proxy app may remember it as missing for up to half an hour: add the domain to the fake-IP filter too, or clear the proxy app’s DNS cache.

items.q: Where can I see what the connector is doing?
items.a: Settings › Connector shows whether cloudflared is installed and running, its version and last exit code, and its log. If something keeps failing, you can export diagnostics there.

items.q: How do I update Loggia?
items.a: Loggia checks for a new version once a day. When there is one, it shows what changed and can download it, install it and relaunch for you. To check right away, click Check for Updates in Settings › About; to stop the daily check, turn off Check for updates automatically there. Your settings and services are kept, and updates are free on both plans. The changelog lists what changed in each version.

items.q: How do I uninstall Loggia completely?
items.a:
1. In Settings › Cloudflare, click Remove Everything… to delete Loggia’s domain records, routes and access protection from Cloudflare.
  2. Quit Loggia and move it from Applications to the Trash.
  3. In Terminal, run launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.useloggia.app.cloudflared, then delete ~/Library/Application Support/Loggia, ~/Library/Logs/Loggia and ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.useloggia.app.cloudflared.plist.
  4. Delete the “Loggia” items in Keychain Access.

privacy.lead: This policy covers the Loggia app and this website: what is collected, who it is sent to, and the choices you have.

sections.body:
To activate, verify or deactivate Pro, Loggia sends the license key and a device label (your Mac’s name plus a short code derived from a hardware identifier) to Dodo Payments over HTTPS. Nothing else is sent.

Loggia has no accounts, no analytics and no servers of its own.

Loggia does not collect or receive the services you publish, your domains, your Cloudflare API token, the traffic that reaches your services, or how you use the app. Everything runs on your Mac or in your own Cloudflare account. Visitors reach your services through Cloudflare, straight to your Mac.

Logs stay on your Mac. Exporting diagnostics creates a file that you send yourself; tokens, license key and your home folder are removed from it.

• Cloudflare: Loggia calls the Cloudflare API with your token to manage tunnels, domain records and access protection in your account. Cloudflare’s own privacy policy applies to your account.
  • GitHub: to download cloudflared and to check for a newer version of it.
  • dl.useloggia.com: to check for a new version of Loggia, once a day unless you turn off automatic checks. The request carries the app name and version, the update framework’s version and your IP address; no system profile is sent.
  • Public DNS: to check that your domains resolve.
  • Dodo Payments: our payment provider and the merchant of record. At checkout Dodo collects your name, email address and billing details under its own privacy policy, and handles invoices, taxes and refunds. Loggia does not receive your payment details.
  • This website: static, with no cookies. It and the downloads are served by Cloudflare, which keeps standard access logs. Visits are counted with Cloudflare Web Analytics, which measures page views and page load times. According to Cloudflare, it uses no cookies or local storage, does not fingerprint visitors and does not collect personal data. The app does not use it.

• Your Cloudflare API token and your Pro license key are kept in your Mac’s keychain.
  • Settings and the service list are kept in ~/Library/Application Support/Loggia; the connector’s log is in ~/Library/Logs/Loggia.
  • The developer can see your purchase record (name, email address, payment ID) in the Dodo dashboard, only to give support and process refunds.

You can deactivate your license in Settings › License at any time. To ask what we hold about you, or to have it corrected or deleted, email support@useloggia.com; we reply within 30 days.

If you are in the EU or the EEA, you also have the rights the GDPR gives you, including data portability and the right to complain to your local data protection authority.
If this policy changes, the date above changes with it.

These Terms of Service are also the license agreement for Loggia. Loggia comes in a free plan and a Pro plan. The free plan is free to use; Pro needs a purchased license key. You are granted a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to install and use official releases of Loggia on Macs that you own or control. The software is licensed, not sold.
The free plan publishes up to 2 services and cannot turn on new access protection. Pro has no such limits. A Pro license covers every 1.x version.

One key can be active on up to 2 of your own Macs at a time. To use it on another Mac, deactivate it in Settings › License on one of the two first. The key is for the purchaser only: do not transfer, rent, lend, share or resell it. If you lose your key, write to support@useloggia.com and we will send it again once we have confirmed the purchase.

To activate, verify or deactivate, Loggia sends only the key and a device label (your computer’s name plus a short code derived from a hardware identifier) to Dodo Payments. If verification cannot connect, Pro keeps working for up to 30 more days.

Loggia sets up tunnels, domain records and access protection in your own Cloudflare account with the token you give it. You are responsible for that account, for your domains, and for the services you make reachable from the internet, including complying with Cloudflare’s terms and applicable law. Loggia does not host your services and does not see your traffic. Your Cloudflare API token and your license key are kept in your Mac’s keychain, and the token is used only to call Cloudflare. Loggia does not send your Cloudflare token, your services or usage data to us.

Without prior written permission of the copyright holder you may not: copy, modify, reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble the software (except where law expressly allows); redistribute, rent, lend, sublicense or sell it; bypass or tamper with license verification; or remove copyright notices.

Loggia checks for new versions once a day, and when you ask, by reading an update feed from dl.useloggia.com; the request carries the app name and version, the update framework’s version and your IP address, and no system profile. A new version is installed only after you confirm it and only if both Apple’s code signature and the update’s own signature verify. You can turn the daily check off in Settings. Updates are free on both plans. An update is covered by these terms unless it comes with its own.

Loggia downloads and runs cloudflared by Cloudflare, Inc. at runtime, and includes Sparkle for updates. They are licensed separately (Apache License 2.0 and MIT), not under this agreement. The list is in the app under Settings › About.

Purchases are processed by Dodo Payments as the merchant of record, which calculates taxes for your region; Dodo’s own terms apply to the payment. Refunds are covered by the Refund Policy. This does not affect rights that the law gives you as a consumer.

If Loggia Pro does not work for you, you can ask for a full refund within 14 days of buying it. You do not need to give a reason.

Email support@useloggia.com from the address you bought with, and include the payment ID from your receipt if you have it. Refunds are issued by Dodo Payments to the original payment method; banks usually take 3 to 5 business days to show it.

Once a refund is done, the license key stops working and Loggia goes back to the free plan. Nothing is taken offline: services you already published keep running. How the free plan treats them is explained in the FAQ. You can buy Pro again at any time.

support.lead: Something not working, or an idea to share? Write to us. We read every message.

sections.body: Write to support@useloggia.com. In Loggia, choose Help › Send Feedback… and a new message opens with your Loggia and macOS versions already filled in.

• What you were trying to do.
  • What happened instead, and any message you saw.
  • Your Loggia and macOS versions, if you did not use Send Feedback.

If something keeps failing, choose Help › Export Diagnostics… (or Settings › Connector › Export…). Loggia saves a zip file and shows it in Finder; attach it to your email. Tokens and your license key are removed and your home folder is shortened to ~. Loggia never sends the file by itself.
The FAQ answers the common questions, including what to do when a service is down. For a refund, see the Refund Policy.
To report a security problem, write to the same address with “Security” in the subject, and please do not post it publicly.
